geography.notes: Available to qualifying residential electric members in Southeastern Indiana REMC service territory.

HVAC and water-heater equipment must meet the efficiency and installation requirements stated on the specific SEIREMC rebate page or form.

geography.notes: Limited to eligible owner-occupied one- or two-family homes in the Town of Babylon.

geography.notes: Limited to new commercial construction projects served by Alameda Municipal Power.

hardRequirements: Project must be commercial new construction in Alameda Municipal Power service territory.
Applicants should contact AMP early in design because the program supports design assistance and new-construction efficiency approaches.
System-specific incentives are limited to eligible lighting and HVAC approaches, while other efficiency projects may require custom review.
Rebate availability and amounts are subject to AMP program rules and funding.
blockers: Do not match high_efficiency_refrigeration_equipment; the current AMP new-construction page does not list refrigeration rebates.

repairs.reasoningNotes: The original refrigeration match is unsupported by the current official AMP page. HVAC and lighting are only appropriate within commercial new construction, not ordinary retrofit replacement.

geography.notes: Statewide Alaska NEVI implementation, with initial corridor deployment focused on Alaska's Alternative Fuel Corridor between Anchorage and Fairbanks and later expansion to communities and other corridors.

hardRequirements: Projects must follow Alaska Energy Authority NEVI solicitation requirements when an application round is open.
NEVI funding is for public EV charging infrastructure under federal NEVI rules, including corridor-oriented fast charging deployment.
Selected sites must comply with applicable federal EV charging standards, operations, data, uptime, and reporting requirements.
Application availability depends on AEA procurement or grant rounds; site selection and award status must be verified for the current round.
blockers: Do not match LED lighting; it is not an eligible retrofit category for Alaska NEVI.
Do not match generic Level 2 EV charging from separate Alaska programs unless a specific NEVI solicitation includes it.
Do not match private residential EV chargers or non-public charging installations.
This record is infrastructure grant support, not a general building energy-efficiency rebate.
repairs.evidenceText: AEA's]( EV pages and FY26 NEVI plan describe Alaska's NEVI deployment as public EV charging infrastructure, initially along the Anchorage-Fairbanks corridor, with program implementation through AEA and federal NEVI requirements.
repairs.reasoningNotes: EV charging is correct, but the category should emphasize public DC fast charging and NEVI infrastructure. LED lighting is a false-positive match. Level 2 charging belongs to other programs unless an AEA NEVI round explicitly includes it.

geography.notes: Statewide Pennsylvania program for eligible projects that meet DCED Alternative and Clean Energy Program rules.

hardRequirements: Applicants and projects must meet DCED Alternative and Clean Energy Program eligibility rules.
Program provides grants, loans, and loan guarantees rather than a rebate for a fixed product list.
Most projects require a matching private investment or equivalent eligible match under program guidelines.
Applications are submitted through Pennsylvania's grants system and are subject to DCED review and funding availability.
blockers: Do not match standalone LED lighting, biomass, or geothermal categories unless the actual project qualifies under ACE as an approved alternative clean energy, efficiency, conservation, or manufacturing project.
Do not treat this loan/grant program as a simple equipment rebate.
Residential-only retrofit matching is not supported by the official program page.
A project must fit the ACE funding categories; general building upgrades without an approved clean-energy or efficiency purpose should not match.
repairs.administrator: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development
repairs.evidenceText: DCED]( describes ACE as grants, loans, and loan guarantees for alternative and clean energy projects, CNG/LNG fueling infrastructure, and energy efficiency or conservation projects by eligible Pennsylvania entities.
repairs.reasoningNotes: The current official program page supports broad project financing categories, not rebate-style matching to individual biomass, geothermal, or LED retrofit types. Confidence is medium because detailed guideline content was not fully readable from the official PDF.

geography.notes: Statewide Utah sales-tax exemption for qualifying purchases or leases by eligible alternative-energy, waste-energy, or alternative-fuel production facilities.

hardRequirements: Purchases or leases must qualify under Utah sales-tax exemption law and the TC-721 Alternative Energy exemption certificate.
Alternative energy electricity production facilities must meet the statutory facility definition, including the required production-capacity threshold where applicable.
Property must be used by or for a qualifying alternative energy electricity production, waste energy production, or alternative energy fuel production facility.
Taxpayer must retain proper exemption documentation and satisfy Utah State Tax Commission requirements.
blockers: Do not match ground-source geothermal heat pumps; the statutory category is geothermal energy production facility equipment, not building HVAC heat pumps.
Do not match LED lighting or ordinary building energy-efficiency retrofits.
Do not match small residential renewable systems that do not meet the statutory alternative-energy facility requirements.
This is a sales-tax exemption, not a rebate or grant.
repairs.evidenceText: Utah's]( current TC-721 form includes an Alternative Energy exemption tied to statutory qualifying alternative-energy electricity production, waste-energy production, and alternative-energy fuel production facilities.
repairs.reasoningNotes: Biomass and geothermal only remain valid when tied to qualifying energy production facility equipment. The original ground-source geothermal heat-pump and LED retrofit matches are false positives.

geography.notes: Statewide New York credit for eligible property used in a New York trade or business.

hardRequirements: Property must be used more than 50 percent in a trade or business in New York State.
Credit is for qualified alternative-fuel vehicle refueling or electric-vehicle recharging property.
Credit amount is generally the lesser of the statutory dollar cap or 50 percent of cost reduced by certain public grants.
Taxpayer must claim the credit using the applicable New York tax form and meet carryforward and recapture rules.
blockers: Battery storage systems are not eligible under this tax credit and should not match.
Do not narrow to Level 2 only; the official credit covers eligible EV recharging property rather than only Level 2 chargers.
Residential chargers without qualifying business use should not match.
Do not match general electrical work except as part of eligible refueling or recharging property.
repairs.programType: Corporate And Personal Income Tax Credit
repairs.administrator: New York Department of Taxation and Finance
repairs.evidenceText: New]( York tax guidance describes a credit for qualified alternative-fuel vehicle refueling and electric-vehicle recharging property used in a New York trade or business.
repairs.reasoningNotes: EV recharging is supported. Battery storage was a false positive, likely from the word storage in tax guidance or forms. Level 2 should not be the only charger category.

geography.notes: Limited to eligible Burbank Water and Power commercial, industrial, municipal, and multifamily common-area electric-service premises.
